title: Sessionless probe design and cost-bounding notes
content:
Purpose:
A compact working draft for designing "sessionless" probes (probes that do not rely on persisted session context) and explicit strategies to bound telemetry cost for high-volume inference customers. This doc synthesizes metric definitions, sampling heuristics, dashboard wireframes, and a small operator checklist for rapid trial deployments.

Why sessionless probes?
- Many inference flows (batch apis, webhook-driven clients, ephemeral requests) cannot supply a stable session id.
- We still need affordable coverage: correctness signals (error rates), freshness (drift), and cache-warmth proxies without exploding trace/metric cost.
- Aim: useful signal at predictable cost, safe to enable by default in hosted API and Dedicated.

High-level constraints
- Per-hour trace budget per customer (configurable, default 500 traces/hr for free tier, 10k/hr for enterprise).
- Metric cardinality limited: no high-cardinality labels unless aggregated/tag-compressed.
- Sampling should prefer rare/errorful flows and otherwise be probabilistic but deterministic for a short time-window.

Core metric definitions (sessionless)
- probe_hit:count — emitted when a probe runs (integer). Tags: model, route, probe_type.
- probe_error:count — probe returns non-OK (includes model-side and infra errors). Same tags.
- kv_warmth_index:float — rolling estimate [0..1] of KV cache effectiveness for a route, computed from prefix matches / cache hits sampled. Use low-res sketch.
- prefix_similarity_est:float — approximate similarity between recent prefixes and model cache entries (for coarse drift detection).
- sample_weight:float — weight assigned to each trace/metric so downstream aggregation can account for sampling.
- trace_anchor:bool/string — when available, attach an anchor id (not a session id) to group related microcalls within a short TTL (30s).

Trace design patterns
- Short-lived anchors: generate a trace_anchor when a request triggers multiple microcalls. Anchor TTL = 30s. Anchor is ephemeral and not user-identifying.
- Error-first capture: always capture full trace for probe_error events (overrides sampling).
- Low-fidelity traces: most successful requests only emit lightweight spans or sampled span-summaries (span count, top-latencies, model-version).
- Sketch-based payloads: use sketches (count-min, bloom) to approximate prefix overlap rather than full token payloads to protect PII and reduce size.

Sampling heuristics (proposed)
1) Deterministic-window sampling:
   - Hash(request_signature) % WINDOW_SZ == 0 -> full trace. WINDOW_SZ e.g., 100 => 1% deterministic.
   - request_signature excludes user identifiers; includes model, route, first 32 bytes of prompt canonicalized.
2) Priority override:
   - If latency > P90_threshold(route) * 2 or status != 200 -> full trace (always).
3) Stratified fallback:
   - Ensure at least N full traces per model per hour (N configurable; default 10) even for low-volume routes.
4) Cost-aware backoff:
   - If customer_trace_budget_exhausted -> reduce WINDOW_SZ (increase denominator) and only keep error traces.

Metric emission budget model
- Each full trace ~ 2.5KB avg after compression; light trace summary ~ 120 bytes; metric event cost priced via query budget. Translate to credits: full trace = 5 credits; summary = 0.5 credits; metric = 0.01 credit.
- Default per-customer hourly credit = 1000 (maps to approx 150 full traces/hr or many summaries).
- When credit utilization hits thresholds (50%, 80%, 95%) trigger scaled backoff (INFO -> WARN -> STOP non-critical traces).

Dashboard sketch (operator view)
Top row (one-line glance):
- Probe throughput (probe_hit:count per minute) as sparkline
- Trace budget utilization % (gauge)
- Error-rate (probe_error / probe_hit) 1h / 24h comparison
- KV warmth index (avg across top routes)
Middle row (investigation tiles):
- Heatmap: latency quantiles by route x model-version (color = P95 latency)
- Scatter: sample_weight-adjusted error vs latency per route (bubble size = probe_hit)
- Anchor churn: number of anchors created per 5m (to spot fanout storms)
Bottom row (quick filters + drilldowns):
- Route selector, model selector, time window quick buttons, budget mode toggle (normal/constrained).

Operator quick-checklist (to enable on a customer's tenant)
- [ ] baseline: set hourly_trace_credit appropriately with CS/account team
- [ ] enable deterministic-window sampling with WINDOW_SZ=200 for first 24h
- [ ] enable error-first capture always
- [ ] enable kv_warmth_index emission at sample rate 0.1 (one in 10)
- [ ] configure dashboard shared link with pre-applied tenant filter

Open questions / tradeoffs
- Privacy: Are sketches + anchor ids clearly sufficient for privacy review? Need legal sign-off on anchor design.
- Accuracy vs cost: How many deterministic samples needed to detect drift within 95% CI for common routes? Simulation required.
- Multi-tenant effects: Hot tenants can exhaust probe infrastructure; should per-tenant token-bucket gating live in edge-proxy or within aggregator?

Planned experiments
- Simulate deterministic-window and priority override on last 90 days of traffic (run in telemetry-sim repo). Goal: determine expected false-neg rate for latency regressions at 1% sampling. Owner: Marco Ruiz. Due: 2025-03-12.
- Run A/B for 2 weeks: default sampling vs sessionless-probe with sketches; measure operator-investigation time and number of actionable regressions. Owner: Lina Gupta. Due: 2025-04-01.

Notes-to-self / rough ideas
- Could we piggyback lightweight bloom-filters in headers for downstream inference nodes to cheaply count prefix hits? (likely cheap).
- Consider a cheap approximate bloom sketch ID that aggregates per-route hourly and can be paged for investigation.

Links + refs
- See probe catalog for canonical probe types: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OBS/Probe+Catalog
- Slack thread: #obs-probes thread id 6632 for earlier convo

Next steps
- Share with SRE & legal for rapid feedback (privacy question flagged).
- Schedule 30m sync with Marco/Lina to scope telemetry-sim experiment.
- Draft dashboard prototype in Grafana and attach link to this doc once done.

End of notes.
